newsitem.title: USA: Nicaragua president urges U.S modify immigration law.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua president urges U.S modify immigration law.

text.p: Nicagarua's president on Thursday urged the U.S. government to modify immigration laws under which thousands of Nicaraguans could be deported from Miami and other cities.
"Is it not possible that the country that helped us fight Communism will help us now?" Arnoldo Aleman asked the audience at a luncheon hosted by the Los Angeles World Affairs Council.
A U.S-backed war between the Contra rebels and Sandinista government forced thousands of Nicaraguans to flee the Central American country in the 1980s.
Changes in U.S. immigration law that took effect April 1, left thousands of refugees from Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador and other countries open to deportation.
"Are we going to violate human rights or not? That's what we're trying to find out," Aleman said Thursday.

Meanwhile, a U.S. district court judge in Miami has refused to dismiss a class-action lawsuit filed in March on behalf of Nicagaruan immigrants who claim the United States has illegally denied them residency.

The lawsuit named as defendants President Bill Clinton, Attorney General Janet Reno and Immigration and Naturalization Service Commissioner Doris Meissner and claimed class-action status on behalf of 50,000 Nicaraguans, most of them living in Miami.
The defendants have a few weeks to respond to the complaint. The lawsuit is just one salvo in a battle between immigrant advocates and the government over the changes to the immigration law.
